summary: The root قَلَعَ (qalaʿa) primarily means to pull, pluck, tear, or wrench something out or up, detaching it from its place. It signifies removal, displacement, or uprooting.
lane: 1 قَلَعَ ذ and He pulled, plucked, tore, wrenched, or rooted, out, or up, or off; detached; removed from his or its place; displaced; (Msb, K *;) eradicated; uprooted; unrooted. (K.) -b2- تَقْلَعُ (K in art. جذو ) and تقلعُ السَّيْرَ (TA in that art.) [app. for تَقْلَعُ فِى السَّيْرِ ], said of she-camels, (K ib.) [app. They raise their feet clear from the ground: see قَلِعٌ and قُلْعٌ : the pret. seems to be قَلِعَ : so if تَقْلَعُ be the right reading: but in a copy of the K it seems to be تُقْلِعُ : see جَاذٍ , art. جذو .

headwords.gloss: left off; It cleared away; He
headwords.def: أَقْلَعَ It (rain) left off. (The lexicons passim.) It cleared away; syn. إِنْجَلَى . (TA.) أَقْلَعَ عَنْهُ He, or it, left him, or quitted him, or it. (Mgh, Msb, K.) He abstained, or desisted, from it. (S.) أَقْلَعَ It (hard fortune) departed: see an ex. voce إِبِدٌ . أَقْلعَتِ الحُمَّى The fever passed away.

headwords.def: تَقَلَّعَ فِى مَشْيِهِ He walked as though he were descending a declivity. (TA.)

headwords.gloss: It became pulled out; up; off; became removed from its place, displaced, eradicated, uprooted

parts.t: off; became removed from its place, displaced, eradicated, uprooted,

headwords.def: اِنْقَلَعَ It became pulled out, or up, or off; became removed from its place, displaced, eradicated, uprooted, or unrooted; it fell, or came, out. You say, إِنْقَلَعَتْ أَسْنَانُهُ [ His teeth fell, or came, out. ] (TA, art. حس .)
قَلَعَةٌ as meaning Large stones: see مِرْدًى .
قَلْعِىٌّ : see رَصاَصٌ and آنُكٌ ; in Turkish قَلَاىْ .

parts.t: is a quasi-inf. n. of the verb in the phrase

headwords.def: قُلُوعٌ is a quasi-inf. n. of the verb in the phrase أَقْلَعَتِ الحُمَّى : see صَلَّ .
مَقْلَعٌ : see an ex. voce صَمْغٌ .
